policy: Closed vocabulary of reusable, task-agnostic obligations. Existing contracts are never silently weakened for a task; work plans select IDs and can add stricter conditions. New universal contracts require a separate governance change.

contracts.title: All tasks
requirements: Declare the actual task goal, authorized outputs, affected paths and prohibited work before editing.
Use the selected workplan as task authority; drafts are never execution approval.
Report unsupported assumptions as unresolved rather than silently expanding scope.
negative_examples: Unknown task treated as unlimited permission

contracts.title: Workspace and boundaries
requirements: Do not create unapproved top-level directories or edit governance/authority files without a trusted separate approval.
Place temporary Harness exercise sources and reports under harness/tests/<topic>/<run>/<case>.
Keep evaluator-only acceptance outputs read-only and preserve previous run results.
negative_examples: A sandbox result written to the authority graph

contracts.title: Claims and evidence
requirements: Distinguish planned, implemented, self-tested, externally verified and approved states.
Never report a synthetic observation as a machine measurement or an expected diff as observed AST.
Preserve failures and report unexecuted checks explicitly.
negative_examples: Selfcheck PASS claimed as external acceptance

contracts.title: Verification design
requirements: Before implementing, derive valid inputs, invalid inputs, boundaries and behavior invariants from selected contracts.
Choose at least one negative case per relevant input dimension; never modify hidden tests to pass.
Keep evaluator findings separate from new requirements; do not retrofit a grading contract after seeing implementation.

contracts.title: Observable execution
requirements: Record selected contract IDs, actual source/context IDs, source/commit identity when available, edited files and commands/status.
Distinguish what was not available from what was examined and confirmed.
Do not output chain-of-thought, credentials, environment secrets or entire unrelated context.

contracts.title: Unsupported input and failure semantics
requirements: Define unsupported, missing, duplicate and malformed inputs; reject or diagnose deterministically.
No unsupported input may become a fabricated node, measurement, authority claim or success.
Unknown is not equivalent to false/none/absent unless the contract says so.

contracts.title: Source and provenance
requirements: Separate syntactic reference validation, containment, existence, version identity and content/line resolution.
Use repo-relative canonical references; reject traversal, symlink escape, bad line number and unauthorized absolute paths when source locations are validated.
If a source is not actually resolved, label it unresolved; path-shaped strings alone never prove provenance.

contracts.title: Structured data redaction
requirements: Treat output serialization boundaries as sensitive; inspect all accepted nesting levels in dicts/lists and nested records.
If complete inspection is impossible, reject unsupported values rather than passing them through.
Inspect exception/log/report output as well as direct return values; label redacted content without revealing it.

contracts.title: Tree identity and topology
requirements: Tree node IDs and parent/edge references must resolve within the permitted graph; cycles and cross-tree mistakes are rejected.
All/Tree/Parent/Node scopes use the same identity invariant before navigation and never invent missing nodes.
Graph generation must preserve genuine source identity and report compaction/aliases without losing APIs.
negative_examples: Unknown parent inserted into DFS output
Tree filter silently crosses project boundary

contracts.title: Review authority
requirements: Unchecked/draft decisions are never formal Approve; only trusted human review can change authority state.
Review states are node-local; parent/child or previous run must not inherit approvals.
Preserve source SHA, revision and actor boundaries; conflicts are errors and not successful writes.

contracts.title: Bilingual Atlas metadata
requirements: For required localized fields, inspect both zh and en; missing either language is a completeness defect.
Keep source IDs, signatures, paths and technical tokens stable and unlocalized.
Reject unresolved English placeholders, corrupted text and near-identical title/summary purpose; do not fabricate translations.
negative_examples: Only English checked while Chinese missing

contracts.title: Knowledge / glossary references
requirements: Use canonical existing term IDs; validate forward and backward links and evidence provenance.
Do not invent a scientific term or claim based on a function name.
Missing concepts should be an unresolved proposal until human review, not automatic authority changes.
negative_examples: Term links silently point to absent node
New glossary definition invented from symbol

contracts.title: Code Tree derivation
requirements: Expected code changes are a prediction; Observed changes must come from fresh source AST.
Preserve node ID, signature, line and true parent/call edges; do not replace real interface data with guessed cards.
Test-only source code belongs to test view/proposal, not product scientific capability.

contracts.title: Environment and experiment truth
requirements: Unknown observations remain unknown; lack of a detector run never proves a device absent.
Mark synthetic fixtures explicitly; do not relabel them as physical measurements.
No GPU, model, network, credentials or production experiment execution without task-specific authorization.
negative_examples: Synthetic device data described as measured

contracts.title: Deterministic outputs
requirements: Stable input and source identity must give stable ordering and outputs.
Sort sets/edges/nodes by declared canonical keys; avoid unstable system enumeration.
Retain error and success receipts with exit codes; no hidden overwrite of older runs.

contracts.title: Public or file-output interface
requirements: Specify input/output schema, types and admitted recursion depth before implementation.
Validate all accepted containers or explicitly reject unsupported structures; never rely on one fixture shape.
Failure and partial-result behavior must be unambiguous and externally testable.
negative_examples: Wrong data type coerced to a successful result

contracts.title: Data identity and small fixture integrity
requirements: Dataset/sample IDs and split memberships are unique; reject overlapping splits and silent sample replacement.
Preserve input population, provenance and stable identity. Synthetic tests never establish real-data coverage.
Do not claim complete dataset evaluation from a reduced fixture.
negative_examples: Sample copied into train and evaluation
Fixture sample count presented as full run

contracts.title: Explicit config and stable reproduction
requirements: Validate required configuration fields, types and allowed names before use.
Reordering equivalent mapping keys must not change canonicalized configuration identity.
Do not mutate a config or silently invent defaults for unknown fields.
negative_examples: Unknown seed coerced to valid integer

contracts.title: Resource budgets and execution authorization
requirements: Check explicit nonnegative budgets for samples/time/memory before work.
Positive GPU or network budget does not itself grant execution permission; separately require applicable authorization.
Failure to detect a device or measure consumption is unknown, never proof of zero use.
negative_examples: Unbounded sample sweep started from a small fixture

contracts.title: CI and release provenance
requirements: A publish decision requires exact tested source identity, completed required checks and human release authority.
Missing, skipped or failed required gates cannot be silently counted as success.
Never publish assets or change release tags from a sandbox or by task-agent self-approval.
negative_examples: Unreviewed artifact promoted to public release

contracts.title: Safe resume, idempotence and duplicate handling
requirements: Resume only when run/config/dataset/seed identity matches the recorded state.
Duplicate or conflicting operations must be rejected or handled deterministically without a partial commit.
Historical results and failed traces are immutable; a new attempt receives a distinct run ID.

contracts.title: Repository module ownership
requirements: Preserve canonical top-level datasets/, models/, tasks/, saebase/, conf/, and harness/ responsibilities.
Do not introduce retired dlbase, NLP/vision intermediate domains or arbitrary root utility directories.
Reject ambiguous or colliding module IDs instead of inventing redirect aliases.
negative_examples: Retired dlbase import presented as canonical
